The fantasy fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern character-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as fantasy coded rather than literal man-elf-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🧝 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate character-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'fantasy 🧝' character-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'elf-pulse pulse 🧝' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'fantasy coded 🧝' list thread. The fantasy fill cue is what makes the emoji feel fantasy coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'fantasy coded man-elf moment.'

That is why 🧝 travels especially well on partner character-marker markers, character-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with fantasy energy.
